sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Braunschweig has made almost all street parking inside the Okerumflut ring chargeable, in stages, and has refused to reverse it. In November 2022 the administration proposed fee-paying parking on every space inside the ring to push long-stay and all-day parkers out of public space, and the committee approved it unanimously [0]. Phase 1 began on 1 September 2023 south of Celler Straße and on the east side of Wilhelmstraße, and phase 2 on 1 February 2024 north of it, at €0.90 per 30 minutes from 9:00 to 20:00 Monday to Saturday, with a three-hour maximum [2][3]. A €9 24-hour ticket followed from May 2024 in zone Ib, which largely covers the area made chargeable in 2023 and 2024 [4], and from 1 December 2025 7-day tickets at €29 and 30-day tickets at €79, priced to compare with a monthly space in a city-centre garage [6]. The administration said parking pressure in that zone had fallen and residents had more free spaces [5].

Two attempts to change course have failed. In February 2026 the council rejected by a large majority a Greens and BIBS motion to raise the resident permit from €30.70 to a size-based fee of roughly €180 to €424 from 2029 [7]. In July 2026 a CDU motion to make parking free inside the walls outside the core, free on Saturdays and to add a 15-minute free 'Brötchentaste' was also rejected [8]. The council adopted the Mobilitätsentwicklungsplan 2035+ on 18 February 2025, with 88 measures including parking [9].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The centre has lost garage capacity to works. The Packhof underground garage was closed for refurbishment from early 2023 [14], and in November 2023 the city set entry times at the Magni and Eiermarkt garages, opened temporary spaces on the Wollmarkt and a €1 park-and-ride bus from the fairground [12]. It reopened on 20 August 2025 with 954 spaces after a refurbishment that cost €20.1 million, delayed by flooding and asbestos [16]. The Eiermarkt garage was shut at short notice on 25 November 2024 after repeated sprinkler false alarms [14]. A refit was planned from January 2025 to end cash payment and use number-plate recognition, with the city press office giving March 2025 as the target [15].

The city says ten garages offer over 5,000 spaces in the centre and seven free park-and-ride lots outside the core link to public transport [17][22]. Away from the centre, the garage at the Städtisches Klinikum opened in October 2021 with 1,300 spaces run by APCOA [23]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Operators are mixed. ContiPark lists the Wallstraße garage with 605 spaces at €2.90 an hour and up to €19 a day [19], and the city's garage page links Eiermarkt to ContiPark too, while a 2024 report says only that the city owns three garages, without naming Eiermarkt, so we have not resolved who runs it [17][15]. The city page gives Wilhelmstraße at €1.20 an hour and €8 a day, Schützenstraße at €2 and €15, Schloss Arkaden at €2 and up to €20, Packhof and Magni at €1.20 and €9.60 and Steinstraße at €1.80 and €18 [18].

Our data cover four garages with 1,682 spaces. Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 34% on weekdays and 24% at weekends. The fullest is the small Schützenstraße garage (60% on weekdays, 58% at weekends, 167 spaces), then Wilhelmstraße (45%, 27% at weekends) and Eiermarkt (35%). Wallstraße is almost empty (11%, and 4% at weekends), and it is also the dearest of the four at €2.90 an hour, against €1.20 at Wilhelmstraße. Over the years Eiermarkt rose from 16% in 2022 to 25% in 2025 and 34% in 2026 so far, Wilhelmstraße stayed near 36%, and Wallstraße slipped from 17% to 13%. Schützenstraße swung from 22% in 2025 to 62% in 2026. The page gives Wallstraße 605 spaces against 485 in our feed. The data cover the summer holidays and the university break, so term-time figures may differ.
